validity.recommendation: No action on existence/classification/operator family/location. See the separate spec entry below for a real length/year/diameter conflict.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED, independent of GEM. This is a real, currently-operating trunk gas pipeline supplying the city of Aktobe from the Zhanazhol field. Three independent, live-verified sources all describe it as an active asset: (1) Forbes.kz, 2022-08-21 (quoting Energy Minister Bolat Akchulakov at a public meeting in Aktobe oblast): 'today the city of Aktobe is supplied with gas from 2 trunk gas pipelines: MG "Zhanazhol-Aktobe", whose design capacity is 80,000 m3/hour, with actual [throughput] 100,000 m3/hour, and "Bukhara-Ural"...'; (2) intergas.kz's current (2026) 'General information' page, which lists 'gazoprovod "Zhanazhol-Oktyabrsk-Aktobe" with loopings' as one of the trunk systems actively operated today under UMG Aktobe; (3) АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия»'s own 2015 annual report (filed with KASE) gives a full system table with a 95.7% utilization rate in 2015 for a line it calls 'Zhanazhol-Aktobe'. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is correct -- every source calls it a 'magistral'nyi gazoprovod' (trunk/main gas pipeline); Forbes' headline additionally calls it a gazoprovod-otvod (branch/lateral off the regional trunk grid), which is a minor terminology nuance, not a misclassification -- GEM classifies structurally identical field-to-city trunk lines elsewhere in this same roster (P3963, P3964, P3965) the same way. DUPLICATE: checked against all 39 rows in the Kazakhstan-gas operating roster -- no other row shares this name, and its length/capacity/endpoints don't shadow any other roster entry (P3945 'Zhanazhol-KS13', a genuinely separate line to a different compressor station, is a different, non-overlapping asset -- confirmed by the 2015 Intergaz annual report, which lists them as two distinct table rows: 'Zhanazhol-Aktobe' and 'Zhanazhol-KS 13', 2007, 156 km -- consistent with P3945's own 157.4 km). ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия»' and Owner 'QazaqGaz' are directionally correct -- Intergaz Central Asia is the company whose own annual report and current site describe this pipeline as one of its own operated assets, and it has operated as a subsidiary within the KazTransGas/QazaqGaz corporate family since 2001 (per its own 2015 annual report's corporate history section); Forbes 2022 additionally shows the Ministry of Energy working jointly with 'AO NK QazaqGaz' on this exact corridor's expansion. I could not find an explicit statement of Owner1%=100.00% anywhere (see fills -- left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate the percentage). Location (Start=Zhanazhol, End=Aktobe, both Aktobe region/Kazakhstan) is CONFIRMED, high tier, consistent across every source.

validity.recommendation: Investigate whether P3944's Length (270.00 km) and StartYear1 (1988) are actually describing the WRONG vintage of this corridor. GEM's own figures trace to a single now-dead academic compilation; two more authoritative, more current, mutually-reinforcing sources put the pipeline at roughly 143-155 km with a 2005 commissioning. At minimum, mark Length/StartYear/Diameter as unresolved pending that check rather than treating the current 270/1988/530 trio as settled. If Intergaz TsA's own current site really does still operate BOTH the original 1988 line and a shorter, later addition under one umbrella name ('with loopings'), P3944 may need to be split into two rows rather than have one number picked.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current Length=270.00 km, StartYear1=1988, and Diameter=530.00 mm all trace to ONE source: I fetched gem.wiki's own article and it names citation [6] -- a January 2013 academic paper, 'Gazoprovody Kazakhstana' (library.tou.edu.kz/fulltext/bibl/b794.pdf) -- as the sole backing for length, year, AND diameter (capacity too, at the now-superseded 0.9 bcm/y). That URL is genuinely DEAD today (confirmed HTTP 404 via direct curl, not a TLS artifact), but I recovered it via a Wayback Machine snapshot (2024-01-13) and read the actual table (verified by rendering the PDF page to an image, not just pdftotext, to rule out OCR error): 'Zhanazhol-Oktyabrsk-Aktobe [4] | 1988 | 270/1 line | 0.9/520' -- i.e. the source itself says diameter 520 mm, not GEM's 530 (a small, likely-typo-level 1.9% gap). That table's own footnote [4] traces to an unlabeled ~2010-2013 'Concept of Gas Transport System Development' PowerPoint of unclear authorship/provenance, and the paper's own concluding sentence explicitly warns: 'the presented analysis shows that numerical data on the characteristics of Kazakhstan's gas pipelines are CONTRADICTORY and require systematization' -- i.e. even this source doesn't claim to be authoritative. Against that single, self-admittedly-shaky compilation, TWO independent, more current, mutually-reinforcing sources disagree: (1) АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия»'s OWN 2015 annual report, filed with the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (kase.kz/files/emitters/INCA/incap_2015_rus.pdf, live, 128pp; verified by downloading and reading with pdftotext -layout plus a rendered-page screenshot of the actual system table) -- this is the ACTUAL PIPELINE OPERATOR's own audited filing, not a secondary compilation -- lists a line it calls (without 'Oktyabrsk') 'Zhanazhol-Aktobe', commissioned 2005, length 143 km, design capacity 0.697 bln m3/yr, 2015 actual throughput 0.667 bln m3 (95.7% utilization); (2) the registry's own GulfPub crosswalk (Tier 2, PE World Map, scraped from QazaqGaz's current corporate 'General information' page, qazaqgaz.kz/en/obshchaya-informaciya) independently returns TWO segments both named exactly 'Zhanazhol - Aktobe', totaling 102.998 + 51.499 = 154.5 km -- in the same ~143-155 km neighborhood as the 2015 filing, not GEM's 270. (GulfPub's route geometry for both segments has poor overlap with GEM's own drawn route, IoU 0.03 and 0.21, so even geometrically these may not trace the identical corridor GEM has mapped.) Capacity is the one field NOT in dispute: GEM's live sheet value (0.70 bcm/y) is well supported -- it matches the 2015 Intergaz filing's 0.697 almost exactly, and independently matches Forbes 2022's stated design figure of 80,000 m3/hour (=0.7008 bcm/yr at 8760 h/yr) -- TWO independent sources agreeing closely, high tier. (gem.wiki's own infobox still carries the STALE 0.9 bcm/y figure from the single 2013 compilation, which the sheet has already correctly moved away from -- no further action needed on Capacity.) My working theory, offered as a lead for Update rather than a settled finding: the 1988-vintage, 270 km, 520mm 'Zhanazhol-Oktyabrsk-Aktobe' line and the 2005-vintage, 143-155 km 'Zhanazhol-Aktobe' line reported by Intergaz TsA's own annual filing may be two different physical assets (an original Soviet-era line plus a shorter parallel/replacement string built in 2005), both still bundled under intergas.kz's current listing ('with loopings' = with parallel loop sections) -- in which case P3944 may be under-representing the corridor (one row where there should be two) rather than simply carrying a wrong number. I did not find any source resolving this cleanly, so I'm flagging it rather than picking a number myself.

fills.researcher_notes: Forbes 2022 (Energy Minister quote) describes it as one of two mainlines CURRENTLY supplying Aktobe with gas, giving both design and actual throughput; intergas.kz's current site lists it among the trunk systems actively operated today under UMG Aktobe. Status=operating confirmed by context on both, per the standing rule that status is inferable and need not appear as a literal token.
Named and consistently described as a 'gazoprovod' (gas pipeline) in every source found; no ambiguity.

Both sources call it a 'magistral'nyi gazoprovod' (trunk/main gas pipeline), consistent with GEM's transmission classification and with how GEM classifies the other Zhanazhol-field lines in this roster (P3945, P3963, P3964).

Zhanazhol field -> Aktobe city, both in Aktobe region, is stated consistently in Forbes 2022 ('gas supply to the city of Aktobe'), the 2013 academic paper's table (Zhanazhol-Oktyabrsk-Aktobe, listed under the 'Aktyubinskaya oblast''/Aktobe system), and the 2015 Intergaz annual report (listed under 'Aktyubinskaya sistema'). The academic-PDF verification passed liveness (200) but fails the automated substring check because it's a scanned/rendered PDF -- manually confirmed by rendering the page to an image and reading the table row directly (see spec concern above).

Intergaz TsA's own 2015 annual report lists a 'Zhanazholskoye' linear-production department (one of 5 LPUs under UMG Aktobe) and repeatedly ties gas volumes on this system to 'gas from the Zhanazhol field'. Single-origin (one company's own filing), so tier=medium rather than high despite being a strong primary source. The PDF liveness check passed (200); the automated content check fails on this large scanned/rendered PDF (a known false-negative pattern) -- manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout, page context around line 452/1329/1691 of the extracted text.

Not filling a ref for 270.00 km -- see the spec concern above. The one source that matches this exact number is a single, self-admittedly-unreliable 2013 academic compilation citing an unlabeled PowerPoint; two more current, more authoritative sources (Intergaz TsA's own 2015 annual filing; GulfPub's scrape of QazaqGaz's current site) independently put the pipeline at ~143-155 km instead. Pairing 270 km with a citation right now would overstate how settled this is.

Same conflict as Length -- see the spec concern above. The 2013 academic paper supports 1988; Intergaz TsA's own 2015 annual filing instead dates a line it calls 'Zhanazhol-Aktobe' to 2005. Leaving unresolved rather than citing either number as settled.

The 2013 academic paper's table, read directly off a rendered page image (not just pdftotext, to rule out OCR error), actually says 520 mm, not 530 -- a small but real conflict with GEM's value. GulfPub's Tier-2 crosswalk gives one matched segment at 21 in (533.4 mm, close to GEM's 530) but the other matched segment at 13 in (330 mm, matching neither), so it doesn't cleanly resolve the question either. Leaving unresolved rather than citing a source that, read carefully, disagrees by 10 mm.

Both refs are the operator's own materials (current site + its own 2015 annual filing), so this is one corporate origin, not two independent ones -- tier=medium rather than high, despite being about as authoritative as a self-attested operator fact gets. Both list this pipeline under UMG Aktobe's operated system.

QazaqGaz's involvement with this corridor is real (Forbes 2022 shows the Ministry working jointly with 'AO NK QazaqGaz' on its expansion, and Intergaz TsA has been part of the KazTransGas/QazaqGaz corporate family since 2001 per its own annual report), but I found no source stating an explicit 100% ownership share for this specific pipeline. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than cite a source for a percentage it doesn't actually state.

summary: P3944 Zhanazhol-Aktobe Gas Pipeline: existence/classification/operator-family/location CONFIRMED via Forbes.kz 2022 + Intergaz TsA's own current site + its 2015 KASE annual filing (no duplicate in the 39-row roster). CONCERN (spec): Length=270km/StartYear1=1988/Diameter=530mm all trace to one dead, self-admittedly-unreliable 2013 academic compilation, while Intergaz TsA's own 2015 annual report (143 km, commissioned 2005) and GulfPub's scrape of QazaqGaz's current site (~154.5 km) independently disagree -- flagged for Update to investigate, possibly a two-vintage-corridor split rather than a single wrong number. Capacity=0.70 bcm/y is well supported (2 independent sources) and needs no change. UNRESOLVED: Length, StartYear, Diameter, Owner% refs.
